quests.instruction: Which word means a relative you might only meet at the very biggest family reunions?
quests.question: Second Cousin
quests.hint: This relative is more distant than the cousins you usually see often.
quests.explanation: Second Cousin means a relative you might only meet at the very biggest family reunions.
quests.funFact: Big family reunions are often the best chance to meet second cousins you rarely see!

quests.instruction: Which word means the son of your child, whether your son or your daughter had him?
quests.question: Grandson
quests.hint: This boy could come from either of your own children.
quests.explanation: Grandson means the son of your child, whether your son or your daughter had him.
quests.funFact: A grandson can come through either your son's family or your daughter's family!

quests.instruction: Your son has a baby girl. Which word describes her, from your own point of view?
quests.question: Granddaughter
quests.hint: This baby is your grandchild, one generation further than your own daughter.
quests.explanation: This is granddaughter rather than daughter — granddaughter is your child's own daughter, one generation further than your daughter.
quests.funFact: The exact same baby girl is a granddaughter to you and a daughter to your own son!

quests.instruction: Which word describes your own parent's aunt?
quests.question: Great-Aunt
quests.hint: She is your grandparent's own sister.
quests.explanation: Great-Aunt describes your own parent's aunt, since she is your grandparent's sister.
quests.funFact: The very same woman is a great-aunt to you and simply an aunt to your own parent!

quests.instruction: Which word describes your own parent's uncle?
quests.question: Great-Uncle
quests.hint: He is your grandparent's own brother.
quests.explanation: Great-Uncle describes your own parent's uncle, since he is your grandparent's brother.
quests.funFact: The very same man is a great-uncle to you and simply an uncle to your own parent!

quests.instruction: This relative is the child of your aunt or uncle, unlike your grandparent's own grandchild through your parent. Which word fits best?
quests.question: Cousin
quests.hint: Their parent is your parent's own sibling.
quests.explanation: This is cousin — the child of your aunt or uncle, connected to you through your parents' generation of siblings.
quests.funFact: Cousins are one of the most common ways children build close friendships within their extended family!

quests.instruction: This word describes only the people you live with, while a broader word could include relatives who live elsewhere entirely. Which narrower, more precise word fits best?
quests.question: Household
quests.hint: This word is defined by a shared address.
quests.explanation: This is household — the word defined narrowly by a shared address, unlike relatives or extended family who may live elsewhere.
quests.funFact: A household is defined by where people live, while family and relatives are defined by how people are related!

quests.instruction: This word could describe your great-grandparents, but it also covers relatives from many more generations back. Which broader word fits best?
quests.question: Ancestors
quests.hint: This word is not limited to just one specific generation.
quests.explanation: This is ancestors rather than great-grandparents — ancestors is the broader word covering relatives from any earlier generation.
quests.funFact: All great-grandparents are ancestors, but not all ancestors are necessarily great-grandparents — some are from even further back!

quests.instruction: Your parents and siblings make up this close group, but your aunts, uncles, and cousins do not count. Which phrase fits best?
quests.question: Immediate Family
quests.hint: This is your smallest, closest circle.
quests.explanation: This is immediate family rather than extended family — immediate family is your closest circle of parents and siblings.
quests.funFact: Immediate family usually means the people who live in your own home with you!

quests.instruction: This word names the diagram itself, while a related word names the people from the past it might show. Which word names the tool, not the people?
quests.question: Family Tree
quests.hint: This word is the chart, not the relatives themselves.
quests.explanation: This is family tree — the diagram itself, while ancestors would name the people from the past shown on it.
quests.funFact: A single family tree diagram can display many different generations of ancestors at once!

quests.instruction: This word names one very specific generation — the parents of your grandparents — rather than every earlier generation in general. Which precise word fits best?
quests.question: Great-Grandparents
quests.hint: This word names one exact generation, not a broad span of history.
quests.explanation: This is great-grandparents rather than ancestors — great-grandparents names one specific generation precisely.
quests.funFact: Naming an exact generation, like great-grandparents, helps make a family tree easier to follow!

quests.instruction: This girl is your sibling's daughter, not your own child's daughter. Which word fits best?
quests.question: Niece
quests.hint: Her parent is your own brother or sister, not your own child.
quests.explanation: This is niece rather than granddaughter — a niece is your sibling's daughter, while a granddaughter is your own child's daughter.
quests.funFact: The generation gap is the key difference: a niece is your own generation's child, while a granddaughter is two generations down!

quests.instruction: This word groups you and your cousins together by age level, rather than by your shared relationship to one grandparent. Which word centers on age, not the grandparent connection?
quests.question: Generation
quests.hint: This word groups people by age level, not by their relationship to one specific person.
quests.explanation: This is generation — grouping people by age level, while grandchildren specifically centers on the relationship to a grandparent.
quests.funFact: You can share a generation with people who are not related to you at all, unlike being someone's grandchild!

quests.instruction: This boy is your sibling's son, not your own child's son. Which word fits best?
quests.question: Nephew
quests.hint: His parent is your own brother or sister, not your own child.
quests.explanation: This is nephew rather than grandson — a nephew is your sibling's son, while a grandson is your own child's son.
quests.funFact: The generation gap is the key difference: a nephew is your own generation's child, while a grandson is two generations down!

quests.instruction: This word could describe a great-aunt, a second cousin, or even a distant relative you have never met. Which word is the broadest?
quests.question: Relatives
quests.hint: This is the widest possible word for anyone connected to your family.
quests.explanation: This is relatives — the broadest word, covering everyone connected to your family, near or far.
quests.funFact: The word 'relatives' is so broad that it can include people you have never even met in person!

quests.instruction: Your aunts, uncles, cousins, and grandparents make up this wider group, beyond your own household. Which phrase fits best?
quests.question: Extended Family
quests.hint: This is the wider circle, not your closest household group.
quests.explanation: This is extended family rather than immediate family — extended family stretches beyond your own household.
quests.funFact: Extended family gatherings are a great way to reconnect with relatives you may not see every day!

quests.instruction: This kind of relative shares your exact same two parents, unlike a cousin who only shares a grandparent. Which word fits best?
quests.question: Siblings
quests.hint: Cousins share a grandparent with you, but this relationship is even closer.
quests.explanation: This is siblings rather than cousin — siblings share your exact same two parents, while a cousin only shares a grandparent.
quests.funFact: Siblings are always part of your immediate family, while cousins are part of your extended family!

quests.instruction: Which word most precisely names a relative one step more distant than the cousins connected through your own parents' siblings?
quests.question: Second Cousin
quests.hint: This relative is one step more distant than the cousins you usually see most often.
quests.explanation: This is second cousin — a relative one step more distant than a first cousin, connected through great-grandparents.
quests.funFact: Some families build entire websites just to track their many second cousins and beyond!

quests.instruction: Which family member is two generations below a grandparent, and is a boy?
quests.question: Grandson
quests.hint: Count down: grandparent, then parent, then this boy.
quests.explanation: Grandson is two generations below a grandparent, and is a boy.
quests.funFact: On a family tree, a grandson is drawn two levels below his grandparent!

quests.instruction: Which family member is a girl who calls you 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa', if you become a grandparent one day?
quests.question: Granddaughter
quests.hint: She is the daughter of your own child.
quests.explanation: Granddaughter is a girl who calls you 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa', if you become a grandparent one day.
quests.funFact: Being called 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa' by a granddaughter is a special milestone many people cherish!

quests.instruction: Which word means a woman who is the sibling of one of your grandparents?
quests.question: Great-Aunt
quests.hint: She is your grandmother's or grandfather's own sister.
quests.explanation: Great-Aunt means a woman who is the sibling of one of your grandparents.
quests.funFact: Great-aunts are part of your extended family, connecting you to an even wider family circle!

quests.instruction: Which family member is one generation above your aunt or uncle, and is a man?
quests.question: Great-Uncle
quests.hint: Count up one more generation from a regular uncle.
quests.explanation: Great-Uncle is one generation above your aunt or uncle, and is a man.
quests.funFact: A great-uncle is part of the same generation as your own grandparents!

quests.instruction: This relative shares one of your grandparents with you, but not your own parents directly. Which word fits best?
quests.question: Cousin
quests.hint: This relative's own parent is your aunt or uncle.
quests.explanation: This is cousin rather than siblings — a cousin shares a grandparent with you, not your own parents directly.
quests.funFact: Cousins are connected to you through your aunts and uncles, rather than through a sibling connection!

quests.instruction: Everyone living at your address counts here, even a family friend who stays with you long-term. Which word is more precise than 'family' in this case?
quests.question: Household
quests.hint: This word is about the shared address, not strictly about blood relation.
quests.explanation: This is household rather than family — household is about who shares your address, which can include people beyond blood relatives.
quests.funFact: Two people can be in the very same household without being related by blood at all!

quests.instruction: Which family member might you need help from a family tree just to understand the connection?
quests.question: Second Cousin
quests.hint: This relationship is distant enough that it can be tricky to trace without help.
quests.explanation: Second Cousin might require help from a family tree just to understand the connection.
quests.funFact: Genealogists — people who study family history — love mapping out connections like second cousins!

quests.instruction: Which family member is a boy who calls you 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa', if you become a grandparent one day?
quests.question: Grandson
quests.hint: He is the son of your own child.
quests.explanation: Grandson is a boy who calls you 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa', if you become a grandparent one day.
quests.funFact: Being called 'Grandma' or 'Grandpa' by a grandson is a special milestone many people cherish!

quests.instruction: Which word means the daughter of your child, whether your son or your daughter had her?
quests.question: Granddaughter
quests.hint: This girl could come from either of your own children.
quests.explanation: Granddaughter means the daughter of your child, whether your son or your daughter had her.
quests.funFact: A granddaughter can come through either your son's family or your daughter's family!

quests.instruction: Which word means an aunt to your own parent, rather than an aunt to you directly?
quests.question: Great-Aunt
quests.hint: This relative is one whole generation further from you than a regular aunt.
quests.explanation: Great-Aunt means an aunt to your own parent, rather than an aunt to you directly.
quests.funFact: This kind of family puzzle helps show how titles change depending on which generation is asking!

quests.instruction: Your grandfather's brother comes to visit. Which word describes him, from your own point of view?
quests.question: Great-Uncle
quests.hint: Add one extra generation of distance to the word 'uncle'.
quests.explanation: This is great-uncle rather than uncle — great-uncle is the brother of your grandparent, one generation further than a regular uncle.
quests.funFact: A great-uncle often has wonderful stories about what your grandfather was like growing up!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the relationship between two people whose grandparents were siblings?
quests.question: Second Cousin
quests.hint: Their shared relative is one generation further back than a regular cousin's.
quests.explanation: Second Cousin describes the relationship between two people whose grandparents were siblings.
quests.funFact: If your grandparent and someone else's grandparent were siblings, the two of you are second cousins!
